## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). A uv workspace of four packages, with ingestion code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest` (spec §4.9).

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes for a chosen range, downloaded once as the baseline | §2.1, §4.2, R1 | A | 1 | About one request per quarter. Volume is measured by Stage 1, because no range is chosen yet (§4.8). |
| O2 | New daily indexes picked up every day, with catch-up after missed days | §4.2, R2 | A | 2 | About one listing and one file per business day. Measured by Stage 2. |
| O3 | Downloaded indexes turned into a clean, deduplicated filing-index table in Parquet | §4.4, §4.6, R3 | A | 3 | Parse time and memory are measured by Stage 1. |
| O4 | The pipeline running on Azure: ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage and Monitor | §4.1, §4.9, R4 | A | 4 | Azure spend is unknown until deployed, and §2.2 gives no cost guarantee. Measured by Stage 6. |
| O5 | Backfill, daily ingestion and reconciliation sharing one downloader, parser and publisher | §4.1, R5 | A | 5 | Engineering time only |
| O6 | Original bytes kept, so a parser change reprocesses without downloading again | §4.3, §4.5, R6 | A | 6 | Storage equal to the raw volume of O1 plus O2 |
| O7 | The quarterly baseline re-checked on a schedule, with additions and changes recorded | §4.2, §4.4, R7 | A | 7 | One re-download of every supported quarter per run (§4.8, weekly) |
| O8 | All SEC traffic from all pipelines kept under one shared request budget | §4.3, R8 | A | 8 | Caps throughput at 3 requests per second (§4.8) |
| O9 | Readers get each quarter through one versioned manifest and active pointer, never partial files | §4.5, §4.6, R9 | A | 9 | Engineering time only |
| O10 | No records lost to errors, and closed-quarter removals held until a hash-bound approval | §4.4, R10 | A | 10 | Operator time for each approval |
| O11 | Schedules, retries and the rate target held as reviewed configuration values | §4.8, R11 | A | 11 | Engineering time only |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Open questions

- The repository holds four scaffold packages (`sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download`, `sec-edgar-index-ingest`, `sec-edgar-ingest`). The spec names only `sec-edgar-ingest` (§4.9), and the root script `sec_edgar:main` has no module. The Stage 1 session settles which packages hold the code.

## Stages

The order follows your ranking except where a dependency comes first. Azure deployment (O4, rank 4) moves after the local stages, because Stages 1–5 can be built and tested without Azure, and the core stage needs real data, not infrastructure.

- [ ] Stage 1: Core — local quarterly baseline to Parquet
      Objective: Download a chosen range of real quarterly indexes and produce the filing-index Parquet table locally.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: nothing; the range and SEC User-Agent are set in the stage session (§4.8)
      Produces: a downloader with the SEC identity, a parser to the §4.5 row contract, stored raw bytes, Parquet output, and specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — every quarter in the chosen range is stored as original bytes with its SHA-256. O3 — a Parquet table for those quarters whose row counts reconcile with the source files. Cost — bytes, request count, elapsed time and peak memory of the real run are recorded in the findings file.
      Leaves out: replay from raw (Stage 2), SEC request budget (Stage 3), versioned publication (Stage 4), reconciliation and withdrawal gate (Stage 5), Azure deployment (Stage 6), scheduling and stated defaults (Stage 7), full validation suite (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Daily ingestion and replay from raw
      Objective: Add daily discovery and catch-up through the same downloader and parser, and reprocess from stored bytes.
      Outcomes: O2, O5, O6
      Consumes: Stage 1's downloader, parser and raw storage
      Produces: daily discovery with source-file checkpoints, replay from raw (§4.5 source manifest records), and specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-2-findings.md
      Exit: O2 — real daily indexes from a handoff date are ingested, and a simulated missed run catches up across a quarter boundary. O5 — backfill and daily ingestion call the same downloader and parser. O6 — a parser-version change rebuilds output with zero SEC requests. Cost — daily volume and run time are recorded.
      Leaves out: SEC request budget (Stage 3), versioned publication (Stage 4), Azure deployment (Stage 6), full validation suite (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: SEC request budget
      Objective: Put every SEC request from every pipeline under one shared budget and one active collector.
      Outcomes: O8
      Consumes: Stage 2's shared downloader
      Produces: SEC request budget, meaning the shared collector lease and rate limiting of §4.3
      Exit: O8 — concurrent backfill and daily runs issue requests from one collector at a time, and the combined measured rate stays at or under the configured target.
      Leaves out: Azure Storage-backed lease in deployment (Stage 6), full validation suite (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Versioned publication
      Objective: Publish each quarter as an immutable generation behind a conditionally updated active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 2's transformed observations
      Produces: versioned publication, meaning quarter generations, manifest.json and the active pointer of §4.5–4.6
      Exit: O9 — a reader that follows the pointer sees only complete generations, and a crash injected before the pointer update leaves the previous generation readable.
      Leaves out: Azure Table Storage pointer in deployment (Stage 6), full validation suite (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly sources, publish safe changes, and hold removals for approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 4's versioned publication and Stage 3's SEC request budget
      Produces: reconciliation and withdrawal gate, with changes.parquet and approval records (§4.4)
      Exit: O7 — a real reconciliation run records its additions and updates, or reports none. O10 — a closed-quarter candidate that removes keys stays `awaiting_approval` until an approval names its hash, and open-quarter absence removes nothing.
      Leaves out: Azure deployment (Stage 6), scheduling and stated defaults (Stage 7), full validation suite (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Azure deployment
      Objective: Deploy the shared worker to Azure with production triggers disabled, and pass the bounded live smoke test.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: the accepted ADR (§7 step 1), and Stages 3–5's SEC request budget, versioned publication, and reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Produces: Azure deployment with ADF pipelines, jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, managed identities and Monitor alerts (§4.1, §4.7, §4.9), and specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-6-findings.md
      Exit: O4 — the smoke test against one archived quarter and one daily index (§7 steps 3–5) passes in an isolated environment, with its replay from raw. Cost — the measured Azure spend and the run metrics of §7 step 4 are recorded.
      Leaves out: scheduling and stated defaults (Stage 7), full validation suite (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling, stated defaults and full validation suite
      Objective: Run the baseline and catch-up, enable the triggers, and complete the §6 suite and the §8 runbooks.
      Outcomes: O11
      Consumes: Stage 6's Azure deployment
      Produces: scheduling and stated defaults, the full validation suite (§6) and runbooks (§8)
      Exit: O11 — the §4.8 values are validated before any network request, and observed scheduled daily and reconciliation runs match their durable reports (§7 steps 6–9). Full validation suite — every §6 CI exit criterion passes.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, and writing-plans copies it verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric over O1–O11, with evidence per verdict: the implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, and deferred_items entries. Every numbered spec requirement R1–R11 is cited by an outcome's `Spec` cell. Unmet outcomes exit as a new stage or as a deferral with a written reason.

---

Seven stages, in your ranking except that Azure deployment (O4) moves to Stage 6 because the local stages do not depend on it: do you approve this partition, so I commit it and hand off Stage 1 to brainstorming?
